senses.definition_en: synonym of cierzo (a north-west wind)

examples.english: PALATINO […] Let's stay still until dawn, for the dew and fresh wind [or dew] will make us sick.
examples.ref: c. 1550, Juan Arce de Otálora, Coloquios de Palatino y Pinciano, Spain:
examples.text: PALATINO […] Estémonos quedos hasta que amanezca, que este sereno y recencio o rocío de la noche nos podrá hacer daño.
examples.translation: PALATINO […] Let's stay still until dawn, for the dew and fresh wind [or dew] will make us sick.

examples.english:
It was the night in which seasonably to the world
comes down from the sky the humid fresh air,
And everyone is in a deeper sleep,
In sweet oblivion, and placid silence:
examples.ref: 1607, Christoval de Messa [i.e., Cristóbal de Mesa], “Libro primero”, in La restavracion de España, Madrid: Iuan de la Cueſta, folio 12, verse 70:
examples.text:
Era la noche en ſazon que al mundo
Baxa del cielo el humedo recencio,
Y eſtan todos en ſueño mas profundo,
En dulce oluido, y placido ſilencio:
examples.translation:
It was the night in which seasonably to the world
comes down from the sky the humid fresh air,
And everyone is in a deeper sleep,
In sweet oblivion, and placid silence:

examples.english: Those mornings you can't enjoy are approaching, as they always come with fresh wind and you might get blocked up.
examples.ref: 1894, Luis Maldonado, Las querellas del ciego de Robliza, page 38:
examples.text: Vienen los amaneceres de que no podéis gozar, porque traen siempre recencio y vus podéis costipar.
examples.translation: Those mornings you can't enjoy are approaching, as they always come with fresh wind and you might get blocked up.

examples.english:
and bodily put up with the north-west win
that blows in the mornings;
examples.ref: 1902, José María Gabriel y Galán, “Cara al cielo”, in Extremeñas:
examples.text:
y aguantal con el cuerpo el recencio
de por las mañanas;
examples.translation:
and bodily put up with the north-west win
that blows in the mornings;

examples.english: Iglesias de la Casa, worried about getting out of the road of his ailments, fighting with punchs against the ungrateful life, with poor temperament, unable to bear with dawn's coolness nor with night's north-west wind;
examples.ref: 1911 June 23, José Sánchez Rojas, “Salamanca”, in La España moderna, number 273, Madrid, page 54:
examples.text: Iglesias de la Casa, preocupado en salir del callejón de sus achaques, luchando á puñadas con la vida ingrata, con un temperamento pobre, que no puede soportar el frescor del alba ni el recencio de la noche;
examples.translation: Iglesias de la Casa, worried about getting out of the road of his ailments, fighting with punchs against the ungrateful life, with poor temperament, unable to bear with dawn's coolness nor with night's north-west wind;

glosses: synonym of cierzo (a north-west wind)
